title: Drafting with a reviewer, assembled
sub: A fixed chain turns bullet points into an outline and checks it covers every one, then a separate checker loops on the draft until it passes a style rubric.

steps.d:
"- Shipped dark mode
- Fixed the sync bug reported by several users
- Raised the free-tier project limit from 3 to 5"

steps.h: Your code asks the model to write an outline
steps.d: "1. Dark mode\n2. Sync fix\n3. Free-tier limit raised to 5"

steps.h: Your code checks the outline against the bullets, in plain code
steps.d:
dark mode: covered · sync fix: covered · free-tier limit: covered
(3 of 3 -- no model call needed for this check)

steps.h: Your code asks the model to draft the email from the outline
steps.d:
"This week we shipped an amazing new dark mode, squashed
the sync bug you told us about, and raised free-tier
projects from 3 to 5."

steps.h: The checker finds a rubric violation
steps.d:
"FAIL: 'amazing' is an unapproved superlative;
style guide requires plain, factual language"

steps.h: The model revises using the checker's own feedback
steps.d:
"This week we shipped dark mode, fixed the sync bug you
told us about, and raised free-tier projects from 3 to 5."

steps.h: The checker confirms the draft now passes
